1. The post copy

Does the November vote decide it?

No. The League City ballot question says so before it asks anything. It opens "As a nonbinding statement of voter preference", then asks whether the police department should keep its license plate reader cameras.

Council called the referendum six to one on August 11th for the November 3rd, 2026 ballot. League City police have installed 55 of them since December 2022. A preference is not an instruction.

Pflugerville ordered its own November 3rd election the same day. Its charter review commission recommends a new Section 2.03 on the city's use of artificial intelligence.

League City's council meets August 25th, 2026 in Council Chambers at 200 West Walker Street. Its agenda for that meeting names no camera item, and public comment there may be general in nature. Pflugerville has a Flock camera lease at $87,500 a year set for August 25th too, unvoted.

#LeagueCity #ALPR #Pflugerville

Notes

The record. Re-verified tx-2026-0024, tx-2026-0072, tx-2026-0073, tx-2026-0003 and tx-2026-0057. Admitted tx-2026-0075, tx-2026-0076 and tx-2026-0077. Withdrew tx-2026-0074 as a duplicate of tx-2026-0048. Corrected a wrong public fact on tx-2026-0048: its how-to-take-part field had said the decision now goes to the voters, the opposite of what the item records, and it now carries the ballot's own nonbinding wording and the public comment route the August 25th agenda provides. The deck. The ballot that decides nothing, seven slides on League City's November referendum and Pflugerville's charter section, both on the November 3rd ballot. The panel cleared it at 7.42 over nine rounds. Two of the closing frame's facts were re-sourced from the meeting's own Legistar agenda, which turned out to name no camera item and to carry a public comment that may be general in nature, so the close names both.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
